So, there is much debate about where this phrase came from. No one really knows where the phrase came from. The most common explanation you would get would come from WW2. Specifically the P-51 Mustang. The Mustang had 9 yards of ammo. Giving them "the whole 9 yards" meant shooting all of your available ammo.

However the phrase is older than that. It is closely related to "the whole 6 yards" recorded in Kentucky and South Carolina in 1907. Which is related to "the whole ball of wax" recorded in 1880.

However the phrase only became widespread after Elaine Shepards Vietnam War novel "The Doom Pussy" (giggity). This was around the 1980's.

Another explanation is the British Vickers machine gun in WW1, but this is clearly false as the Vickers standard belt of ammunition was 250 rounds, or 7 yards. There are so many explanations of the phrase, and none of them are actually accepted.

My conclusion, then, is that it must have evolved organically on its own. It's just another way of saying "give it your all". We will probably never have an explanation of where the phrase originated.
